# S296 — Resume a stopped run from its worktree, and continue at the stage it stopped

*Proposed.* The owner can continue a run that ork stopped, from the work in its worktree, with the project's current settings. `ork retry RUN [--rounds N]` (owner decided 2026-11-05: no new verb) accepts a stopped, uncommitted run whose worktree and branch are intact: it reloads the project from the registry, grants N more implementer rounds, begins a new ledger run and re-enters the checks (or `implement` when no implementer round has run, below), so a fixed check command takes effect at once and a green check goes on to review. Owner decisions, 2026-11-05: any uncommitted run stopped after setup can be resumed (named then: the third gate FAIL, an owner stop, and the round limit; since S294 landed the round limit pauses instead of stopping, and the code also stops on an owner reject, a role with no fallback left and a blocked landing); a dismissed run can be resumed and resume clears its dismissal; N defaults to 2; a resume begins a new slicer relay run and the stopped one stays ended as failed. A stopped run already does not block `ork projects set` (verified in the code below), so that part of the request needs no change here.

Owner decision, 2026-11-05 (S295 Q1, option (a)): a run that S295 paused at setup because its check command failed verification is fixed by `ork stop ID`, `ork projects set PROJECT --check CMD`, then `ork retry ID`, which resumes it through this slice. Such a run has a worktree and a ledger run but no implementer round. So the resume enters `implement` (not `checks`) when no implementer round has run, and `stop` of a paused run records the paused step (`pending.state`) as `stopped_from`. S295 depends on this slice.

**Findings:** 2026-11-05, prism-ui: ork retry on ork-20261105-160022-7f6e (U41, stopped by the round limit) answered 'run is not paused with a pending step; use ork stop' (internal/daemon/runs.go:1015-1020). The way on was ork dismiss and a new ork run, which reused the worktree with the work (DocBuildTests.cs still there; ensureWorktree, internal/engine/states.go:705-741). Wanted: ork retry (or ork resume) of a stopped run that reloads the project settings, grants N more rounds and continues from the worktree. The owner also saw ork projects set refused while the run sat stopped; the code counts stopped as final (runrec.IsFinal, record.go:39), so that refusal must have named other runs (not verified). Related: S282, S255, S265. · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-07** — Owner decision 2026-11-07 (interactive answer in the relay session), Q1: option (b). ork run and ork wave start on an item whose newest run is a resumable stopped run auto-resume that run when the worktree's tree hash equals the last implementer round's tree_sha256 (S294); otherwise they start fresh and say so. This replaces the recommended (a). The hash rule, the message wording and the interaction with a dismissed run are for the implementer to settle in the spec's terms and list under Owner needed if unclear.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** starting at the stopped stage when a relaunch reuses an unchanged diff (S282; this slice re-enters the checks, or `implement` when no implementer round has run); the round pause and the new cap (S294); the busy rule for paused or running runs (S265 Q5); resuming a run that setup stopped before its worktree existed, or a committed run (a run paused at S295's setup check and then stopped by the owner is resumable); deleting a dismissed run's files.

## Why

Owner evidence, 2026-11-05 (prism-ui): `ork retry ork-20261105-160022-7f6e` on U41, stopped by the round limit, answered "run is not paused with a pending step; use ork stop". The only way on was `ork dismiss RUN` and `ork run` on the slice again. The new run reused the worktree with the work in it (owner verified that `DocBuildTests.cs` was still there). The run records agree: `ork-20261105-160022-7f6e` (U41) and `-03e0` (U30) are `stopped` and dismissed, and `ork-20261105-162303-1480` (U41) and `ork-20261105-162357-789e` (U30) were started after and are `committed`. The owner also reported that `ork projects set` refused while a stopped run sat there; the code below does not count a stopped run as unfinished, so the refusal must have named other runs of the project (not verified: the refusal text and the other runs' states at that time were not found in the records or the daemon log).

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-05; re-anchored 2026-11-07 at a1114e2, after S294 landed):

- `ork retry` refuses anything but a paused run with a pending step: `MethodRunRetry` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1016-1027`) and `Engine.RetryNote` (`internal/engine/engine.go:471-477`, "the slice is not paused"). `TestRunRetryWrongState` (`internal/daemon/retry_test.go:165`) pins the message and the `ork stop` hint.
- S294 (done) already gives this slice the round grant. `ork retry RUN --rounds N` exists (`internal/cli/run.go:220-238`, usage at `internal/cli/cli.go:83`), the wire carries `RunAction.Rounds` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:73`, 0 means 2), the record keeps the durable grant in `round_limit` (`RoundLimit`, `internal/runrec/record.go:272`), and the pending kind `rounds` (`PendingRounds`, `record.go:146`) is the red-round pause. `RetryNote` grants rounds only at a `rounds` pause today (`engine.go:493-495`). This slice reuses the flag, the wire field and `RoundLimit`; it adds no copy of them.
- `stop` (`engine.go:558-580`) sets `StateStopped`, the reason, clears `Pending` and the queued questions, and ends the ledger run with outcome `stopped` and steps `fail`. It does not record the state it stopped from. It keeps `Feedback`; since S294 `bumpRound` stores the feedback before it pauses (`internal/engine/states.go:179-182`), so an owner stop at a `rounds` pause leaves the last failing check log on the record.
- Stops that leave a resumable worktree: the third gate FAIL (`states.go:662`), an owner stop (`Engine.Stop`, `engine.go:544-551`), an owner reject (`engine.go:422`), a role stop with no fallback left (`internal/engine/round.go:222`, `:496`) and a landing that stays blocked (`internal/engine/land.go:195`). The round limit no longer stops a run: since S294 it pauses with kind `rounds` (`states.go:157-189`), and `ork retry --rounds N` already continues it. A setup stop (`states.go:31-34`) has no worktree to resume, and `StopQueued` (`engine.go:617-623`) stops a run that never started.
- `dismiss` only stamps `DismissedAt` on a stopped run (`runrec.Run.Dismiss`, `internal/runrec/store.go:266`; `dismissRun`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:1228-1260`); it keeps the record, the worktree and the branch.
- `ork run` on the same item reuses the worktree because `ensureWorktree` (`internal/engine/states.go:791`) accepts an existing path whose branch and common git dir match. That is why the owner's relaunch kept the work, and why it restarted at round 1 (the S282 report, absorbed below).
- The busy rule: `setProject` refuses when `unfinishedRunsLocked` returns IDs (`internal/daemon/handlers.go:587-593`); `unfinishedRunsLocked` (`runs.go:1263-1281`) lists runs whose state is not final, and `runrec.IsFinal` (`internal/runrec/record.go:39`) counts `stopped` and `committed` as final. So a stopped run does not block `projects set` today, and a resumed run must re-enter that rule (it becomes unfinished again).
- After a daemon restart a stopped run is not managed: recovery skips final runs (`internal/daemon/runs.go:228-237`), and `ownerRunReply` answers "no run ID" for a run not in the manager (`runs.go:925-942`). `loadFinishedEngine` (`runs.go:1163-1180`) already opens a stopped or committed run from the store and builds its engine with `engine.Load` and the registry entry as it is now; a resume can use it. The owner's case got "not paused" because the daemon had not restarted since the stop.
- Owner actions bypass the project caps: admission happens only in `startRun` (`runs.go:572`, `hasRoomLocked`, adj 122). A resume through `ork retry` would do the same unless the build adds a check; this slice does not change that rule.
- `ensureWorktree` (`states.go:791`) creates the worktree with `git worktree add -b` when the path is missing. That fails when the branch still exists, so a resume must first check that the path exists rather than rely on `ensureWorktree`.
- A started engine keeps the project as it was at the start (`engine.New` with `cfg.Project`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:579-580`); a daemon restart reloads unfinished runs with the registry as it is then (`engine.Load`, `runs.go:246`, `:263`; `Load`, `internal/engine/engine.go:294`). A resume must build its engine from the registry entry as it is at the resume, or a fixed check command does not reach it.

Related: S255 (retry restarts the vendor chain), S265 (busy rule), S293, S295 (depends on this slice).

Absorbed from S282 (retired into this slice on 2026-11-07). S282's report, wave 7, 2026-11-04 (slicer s313): a stopped run could not be retried, so the orchestrator relaunched it with `ork wave start`. The new run started the implementer at round 1 again (claude/haiku, about 30 minutes) although the worktree already held a finished, test-green diff; after the reviewer round failed (S280) the second relaunch did the same. S282 asked that a relaunch whose worktree diff is unchanged since the last green check start at the stage that stopped (review or gate), keep the earlier reports, and ask the owner only if the diff changed; its open point was how ork proves the diff is unchanged. What still holds after this slice's resume: `ork retry` of the stopped run replaces the relaunch, keeps the run's reports, and enters `checks` (or `implement` when no implementer round ran) instead of implementer round 1, so a green diff goes from checks to review without a new implementer round. S294's `roles[].tree_sha256` (`internal/runrec/record.go:51`) now records the implementer's tracked diff per round, which answers S282's open point if a relaunch is ever to detect an unchanged diff. Whether `ork run` or `ork wave start` on an item whose newest run is a resumable stopped run should itself resume it is open (Q1 under Open owner questions).

## Failing tests

In `internal/engine/engine_test.go`:

- `TestResumeAStoppedRunReentersChecksWithMoreRounds`: the run is stopped by the owner after a red round (since S294 the round limit pauses, so use an owner stop at the `rounds` pause). The test makes the check green and resumes with 2 rounds. The run re-enters `checks` (no implementer round first), goes green and reaches review; the worktree file from round 2 is still there; `RelayBegin` ran a second time. Fails first: "the slice is not paused".
- `TestResumeRedChecksStartsAFixRoundWithTheLastFeedback`: as above but the check stays red; the next implementer brief holds the "Checks failed" section with the new log; the run pauses with the `rounds` kind after the granted rounds (S294), and `round_limit` is the resumed round plus the grant.
- `TestResumeRefusesACommittedOrSetupStoppedRun`: a run stopped at setup (no worktree) and a committed run are refused with one line each.
- `TestResumeWithNoImplementerRoundEntersImplement`: a run with a worktree and a ledger run but no implementer round (paused before round 1, as S295's setup pause does, then stopped by the owner; `stopped_from` is `implement`) is resumed. Implementer round 1 runs first with the first-round brief, then the checks; no check runs before round 1. Fails first: "the slice is not paused"; after the stopped branch exists, a resume that always enters `checks` fails it.
- `TestResumeUsesTheCurrentCheckCommand`: the project's check command changes between the stop and the resume; the resumed checks run the new command (`checks[]` row names it).

In `internal/daemon/retry_test.go`:

- `TestRunRetryResumesAStoppedRun` (the wire accepts `stopped` and `rounds`; the managed run is busy, then the record is unfinished).
- `TestRunRetryResumesAStoppedRunAfterARestart` (a stopped run on disk that the manager did not load is resumed, not answered "no run"). Fails first: "no run ID".
- `TestRunRetryWrongState` keeps refusing `implement` and `awaiting-approval` with the `ork stop` hint.
- `TestProjectsSetIsNotBlockedByAStoppedRun` (guard of today's behavior: a stopped run is final; `setProject` succeeds).

## Implement

1. Tests first. Confirm each fails for the reason given (the busy guard passes today; keep it).
2. `stop` records `stopped_from` (the state when it stopped; for a paused run, its `pending.state`, so a run stopped at S295's setup pause records `implement`). `bumpRound` already stores the feedback before its `rounds` pause (S294, `states.go:179-181`); do not change it.
3. A run is resumable when it is `stopped`, has no commit, `stopped_from` is not `setup`, its worktree path exists, and `ensureWorktree` accepts that worktree and branch (check the path first: `ensureWorktree` would try to create a missing one).
4. The daemon opens the run from the store when the manager does not hold it (after a restart), with `loadFinishedEngine` (`runs.go:1163`). It refuses a resume while another run of the same item is unfinished (the relaunch case), then rebuilds the engine from the current registry entry (`engine.Load`), and calls the engine's resume.
5. The engine's resume: clear `DismissedAt`, set `RoundLimit` to the round plus the grant (default 2), begin a new ledger run (`RelayBegin`), set state `checks`, or `implement` when no implementer round has run (no `roles[]` row for the implementer; owner decision 2026-11-05, S295 Q1), and `advance`. Red checks go through `bumpRound` as usual; the limit is `RoundLimit`, and reaching it pauses with kind `rounds` (S294).
6. The CLI: `ork retry RUN [--rounds N] [TEXT]` (flag from S294) accepts a stopped run. The status `next:` hint of a resumable stopped run says `ork retry ID --rounds N`.
7. Docs and CHANGELOG in the same diff.

## Open owner questions

The owner answered the 2026-11-05 questions; the lead records those decisions.

Q1 (open, 2026-11-07, from the S282 merge): should `ork run` or `ork wave start` on an item whose newest run is a resumable stopped run resume that run instead of starting a new one at round 1?
- (a) No auto-resume. The start refuses with a one-line hint `ork retry ID [--rounds N]` while that run is resumable (dismissing it still allows a fresh start). One path to continue, no new rule.
- (b) Auto-resume when the worktree's tree hash equals the last implementer round's `tree_sha256` (S294); otherwise start fresh and say so.
- (c) Keep today's behaviour (a fresh run at round 1 in the reused worktree).
Recommendation: (a). The resume in this slice covers S282's case without a second entry point, and a refusal with the exact command is cheaper than a hash rule.
